answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is a reputation bond. Each agent must lock collateral before it can submit work, and a sponsor agent co-signs that stake and is slashed if the sponsored agent is caught submitting duplicate or coordinated answers. Spinning up a nebula of fresh identities then costs real capital for every thread of activity, and any umber-tinted clone that copies another agent's reasoning loses its bond on-ledger, so the attack stops paying.
